subject.title: Feature: Add 'private' groupPolicy option for Slack channels

question: Should Slack private-channel membership, including Slack Connect/private shared-channel caveats, be accepted as a supported authorization boundary for Slack groupPolicy?
rationale: The code shape is bounded, but the issue changes access-control semantics for agent/tool triggering and automation should not decide that trust boundary.

options.title: Approve Slack-Scoped Private Mode
options.body: Add `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned routing, slash/action/read authorization, docs, security audit behavior, tests, and unchanged defaults unless separately approved.

options.title: Reject Private-Channel Boundary
options.body: Keep explicit Slack channel ID allowlists as the only non-open group authorization mode and document private or shared channels as insufficient trust boundaries.

options.title: Defer To Broader Access Design
options.body: Track this under a broader channel authorization design if maintainers want cross-channel semantics instead of a Slack-specific policy value.

recommendation.title: Approve Slack-Scoped Private Mode
recommendation.body: Add `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned routing, slash/action/read authorization, docs, security audit behavior, tests, and unchanged defaults unless separately approved.

likelyOwner.reason: He already reviewed this exact issue and has the strongest visible history on the Slack/security decision path.
